descriptionChirho: Feminine noun denoting a field or cultivated agricultural land, often appearing in poetic and prophetic contexts describing fertile terrain or its devastation. All four clusters represent the same noun in different grammatical environments: with article, with prepositions (ב ,מן), singular and plural construct forms. Multilingual evidence is consistent: Arabic حُقُول/حَقْل (fields/field), Spanish campos/campo (fields/field), Korean 밭/들 (field/fields), Hindi खेत (field), Swahili mashamba/shamba (farms/field). No semantic distinction exists between clusters -- only morphosyntactic variation of the same agricultural term.
